summary: Mulholland Point Light, Campobello Island: a wooden tower lit in 1885 at the Lubec Narrows, kept by the Parkers and A. F. Newman, decommissioned in 1963 and now in a park.

structures.type: octagonal wooden tower, post and timber-framed, cedar shingles; red iron lantern
structures.note: Total 13.4 m (44 ft) to the top of the lantern; 9.7 m tower plus 3.7 m lantern (marker). The record gives 13.0 m.

staffing.note: Last keeper per Lighthouse Friends: A. F. Newman (1926 to 1963)

access.note: Grounds open to visitors in Roosevelt Campobello International Park; tower closed. Reached by crossing the Roosevelt Memorial Bridge from Lubec, through the customs station.

events.note: Tower completed, 44 ft from base to the vane on its lantern
Fixed white light first exhibited; visible 13 miles (Lighthouse Friends)
Department report proposes removing the light to Cherry Island; the sources do not show the move was made, and later reports still list Mulholland Point
Light discontinued after the Roosevelt Memorial Bridge's navigation lights took over
Tower and shed sold to Campobello resident Clifford Calder
Look family donates the lighthouse to Roosevelt Campobello International Park in memory of Clifford Calder (4 Dec 1984 per Lighthouse Friends)
US Corps of Engineers emergency shore-line protection project at the point
Restoration completed by the NPS Cultural Resource Center, Boston, Building Conservation Branch

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1885 as the build year. Lighthouse Friends says the tower was completed in 1884 and the light first exhibited in 1885. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: (1) Thin station: no storm, wreck or rescue at the light is sourced. Searches of the Canadian Marine reports 1900 to 1924, and of the US Life-Saving Service and Lighthouse Board corpus for Lubec Narrows, found none tied to this light. Chronicling America: 'Mulholland light' (no Maine hits; national noise), 'Mulholland point' with Campobello in Maine papers (0 hits), 'Lubec narrows' in Maine papers (72 hits, mostly unrelated; not read further). Storms and rescues left out. (2) Light data disagree: visibility 13 miles (Lighthouse Friends; the 1885 description in Sunrise via Tides) against 4 miles for the lens (marker 54894). Focal height: record gives 20 m (66 ft); Sunrise gives 60 ft (18 m) for the light itself in 1885. Not resolved; the focal-height figure is not in facts. Tower height: record 13.0 m, marker and Lighthouse Friends 13.4 m (44 ft), corrected. (3) Keeper dates are from Lighthouse Friends; the Department's 1912 report table (year ended 31 March 1911, printed p. 240) confirms Alvin Parker on the Mulholland Point row. The OCR puts the two columns apart, so the match was checked on the page image (scan 247): the Mulholland Point row carries Alvin Parker, June 13, 1901. No corpus check for Malachi Parker or A. F. Newman (Newman is after 1924 and not in the corpus). (4) The Cherry Island proposal (1901): the sources do not say whether it was carried out; the light stayed at Mulholland Point at least to 1911 per the tables, and to 1963 per Lighthouse Friends. (5) Sunrise County Architecture is cited second-hand through the Tides Institute catalogue entry, not read in the book. The two markers are read as transcribed on Historical Marker Database. (6) Named private people: Clifford Calder (a 1963 purchaser, named in the 1984 donation to the park) and the Look family (donors) appear only as the marker, Lighthouse Friends and the catalogue print them, with no further personal detail. (7) Roosevelt's Halsey anecdote (quoted in Lighthouse Friends) not reproduced. (8) Bridge name: marker has 'Roosevelt Memorial Bridge'; Lighthouse Friends has 'F.D.R. Memorial Bridge'. The story uses the marker's form. (9) The record's agency field: the park owns the light since 1984; the Coast Guard operated it until 1963. (10) No photos proposed. (11) The story's Sunrise County Architecture figures reach the reader only through the Tides Institute catalogue, which the story footnotes as second-hand.
